That organizational approach reflects a crucial principle in optimization problems—making the most impactful choices first often leads to the best outcome. By sorting based on units per box, you ensure that every box you select maximizes the units loaded onto the truck given the constraint.

This method is an example of a "greedy" algorithm, which is grounded in always taking the currently best option, hoping that this leads to the global optimum. Greedy algorithms are effective for certain problems where making locally optimal decisions at each step also results in a globally optimal outcome. Keeping this idea in mind can help you not only with this problem but with many similar maximization challenges in programming.
